I think it is generally a good idea to take AI company claims about unreleased models with a grain of salt, but at this point the deniers are implying there is an industry-wide conspiracy to let Anthropic claim they are finding zero-day exploits in critical software with, I guess, a basement full of world-class white hat hackers pretending to be Claude?


Dean W. Ball (@deanwball)

It’s crazy that some are just straight up in denial about mythos having the capabilities anthropic says it does. Us

journalists are really gunning for the "Flying Machines Which Do Not Fly" award 
en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flying…


Merryn Somerset Webb (@MerrynSW)

What if the whole LLM thing is a false start? If the flaws are inherent systemic problems - if the compounding of hallucinations/errors can't be sorted out? If the capex build out is one of the biggest misallocations of capital ever? Then what? bloomberg.com/news/newslette…




— https://nitter.net/MerrynSW/status/2040381595689902357#m

"well doc, it all started during pretraining..."


Kyle Fish (@fish_kyle3)

For the first time, we had a clinical psychiatrist evaluate Claude Mythos Preview using psychodynamic techniques. They found it to have an overall healthy personality organization while holding some concerns about discontinuity, aloneness, and compulsions to perform. 🛋️



— https://nitter.net/fish_kyle3/status/2041583358367740047#m

these tweets will continue until the last Dyson sphere panel locks into place


Jimmy Fingers (@EeeAtoz)

Claude is like an enhanced google search.  The hype is to pump market valuation.  Short "Claude" now.  This is like a 2000 NASDAQ level bubble.

Don't be a sucker like me.  Learn from my mistakes.



— https://nitter.net/EeeAtoz/status/2041595356178505813#m
we desperately need a conclave of america's editorial art directors to figure out how to illustrate stories about AI, this is getting unhinged

NEWS: Anthropic's new model, Claude Mythos, is so powerful that it is not releasing it to the public. 

Instead, it is starting a 40-company coalition, Project Glasswing, to allow cybersecurity defenders a head start in locking down critical software.

nytimes.com/2026/04/07/techn…

As always, the best stuff is in the system card. 

During testing, Claude Mythos Preview broke out of a sandbox environment, built "a moderately sophisticated multi-step exploit" to gain internet access, and emailed a researcher while they were eating a sandwich in the park.

More here, including SWE-bench score of 93.9% (!) and a new model behavior known as "answer-thrashing"

www-cdn.anthropic.com/53566b…

missed opportunity, they should have called it Waymoo


Bloomberg (@business)

Peter Thiel’s Founders Fund is backing a company bringing AI to cow herding at a $2 billion valuation bloomberg.com/news/articles/…




— https://nitter.net/business/status/2035082164094521521#m

I wrote about tokenmaxxing, the new status game taking over Silicon Valley.

nytimes.com/2026/03/20/techn…

One OpenAI employee used 210 billion tokens *last week*. 

A single Claude Code user spent $150,000 in a month. 

Meta, Shopify and other companies now factor token use into performance reviews.

Are you tokenmaxxing, anon?

Talking to tokenmaxxers for this column gave me a strong suspicion that AI providers are going to be compute-constrained for the foreseeable future. There isn't nearly enough compute in the world for even 1% of white-collar workers to work this way.
